# Corpus cross-references

Which cataloged publications cite which, across all 46 entries in
`literature/refs.bib`. Generated by `uv run scripts/build_xrefs.py` from the
parsed Markdown in `literature/corpus/`; regenerate after adding a publication.
**Do not edit by hand.**

304 edges. A number in parentheses is how often the citing paper *names* the
cited one in its prose — a reference-list row scores 1, a paper argued with
scores much higher. That gap is usually the interesting part.

## Read this before quoting any number here

- **Citation is not comparison, and neither is endorsement.** That A cites B says
  nothing about whether A benchmarks against B, agrees with it, or refutes it.
  Only reading the passage settles that.
- **In-degree is confounded by age.** A publication from the last few months has
  had no time to be cited, so its zero means *too new*, not *ignored*. The two
  kinds of zero are separated below; do not conflate them.
- **This is corpus-internal.** Counts are citations from within these
  46 publications, not from the literature. A work the field leans on
  heavily will still score low here if the corpus does not happen to contain
  the papers citing it.
- **Years are the cataloged version's.** An entry upgraded from preprint to
  journal carries the journal year, so a paper may legitimately cite something
  that looks newer than itself — it cited the preprint.
